body:
From the harness discussion on task:30881953fb66677f (note 8). When the MCP `solace` tool gets an argument of the wrong type, it quietly treats it as missing. The agent then gets nothing, or an error that misleads it.

### Known cases
- `options` sent as a JSON string (`"[\"A\",\"B\"]"`) is read as an empty list. The `task ask` reaches the human **with no options**, and nobody is told.
- `text` sent as an object (strategy runs do this) is read as missing, and the error talks about "new code".
- An `old` or `reason` that isn't a string is read as missing.
- `command` sent as a list of lines is read as empty, and the reply is "No command given" plus the **whole reference** (thousands of tokens).

### Change
- **Repair** only when there's just one possible meaning: parse an array that came as a JSON string, serialize an object sent where JSON text is expected, unwrap a one-item list sent where a string is expected, join a `command` list into lines. Each repair adds a line to the reply, e.g. `repaired: options was a JSON string; send an array`.
- **Refuse** any other wrong type, naming the argument and the type expected, and run nothing (the same way E7015/E7017 refuse).
- A truly empty `command` gets a one-line usage and a pointer to `help`, not the whole reference.
- Record each repair and refusal as a step in the run log, with a stable code, so counts per model can be read later.
- Keep the tool schema as simple as it is now (no `anyOf`).
- Record the rule as a decision: repair syntax, never guess intent, always say what was repaired.

### Tests
One for each case above, plus: a correct call is unchanged, and a repaired call shows its `repaired:` line.

### Limit
Claude Code checks arguments against the schema before they reach Solace, so most of these fixes help Codex and other agent programs.
title: mcp: repair or name wrong-type arguments
